about_us_page.title: Built by entrepreneurs, for entrepreneurs
about_us_page.subtitle: We know what it takes to build a business — because we're doing it ourselves. This space exists so you never have to work alone again.
about_us_page.story_text: As entrepreneurs, we tried everything: home offices where loneliness kills motivation, corporate coworkings full of people on someone else's payroll, and coffee shops where you can't take a call. We wanted a space surrounded by people who think like us — who understand the highs and lows of building something from scratch. So we built it.
about_us_page.craft_title: A space made for focus, not flair
about_us_page.craft_text: Every detail was chosen by founders who work here daily. IKEA Markus chairs — tested with our own backs through 8-hour days. Coffee rotated monthly from local Tallinn roasters, because bad coffee makes bad decisions. Fiber-optic Wi-Fi, because a spinning loader during a client call is not an option. Warm lighting, real plants, quiet zones. None of this was the cheapest option — it was the right one.
about_us_page.community_text: We deliberately keep the space small — six to ten people on a typical day. Everyone here runs a business: SaaS founders, consultants, agency owners, e-commerce entrepreneurs. We review every application so the quality of the room stays high. The result: real conversations, real partnerships, and zero small talk about the weather.
about_us_page.mission_text: To prove that where you work shapes how you work. A room full of entrepreneurs creates a different energy than a room full of strangers. We're building the workspace we always wished existed in Tallinn — and keeping it exclusive enough that every seat matters.
about_us_page.boardgames_note_text: We're serious about games too. After 18:00 and on weekends, the space transforms into Tallinn's most extensive board game club. But during work hours, business comes first.
about_us_page.invitation_text: Tell us about your business and what you're building. We review every application personally and get back to you within 1–2 days.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.content:
# Do I need a membership to work here?
You can use day passes or choose a monthly membership.

# What are your opening hours?
Monthly Members: 24/7
Day Pass Users: Monday to Friday: 9:00-18:00

# How do I get access after hours?
Via personal key card / code.

# Can I bring guests?
Yes, guests are allowed for a limited time and must be registered.

# Is high-speed internet included?
Yes, enterprise-grade Wi-Fi. Optic fiber connection.

# What membership plans do you offer?
Daily, weekly, monthly, and team plans.

# What is included in the membership?
Workspace, internet, utilities, coffee/tea, cleaning, community events.

# Are there long-term discounts?
Yes, for 3-month, 6-month, and annual plans can be discussed.

# Is the space pet-friendly?
Small, well-behaved pets are allowed. Please inform us in advance.

# What is your cancellation policy?
14-day notice for monthly plans

# Can I use the address for company registration?
Yes, virtual office and legal address services are available.

# Is the space secure?
24/7 CCTV, access control, and personal lockers (coming soon).

# Can I try the space before committing?
Yes, with a free tour or trial day.

# Where are you located and how do I get there?
We are located at Kivimurru 34. Easily accessible by public transport and bike. Not far from T1 center.

neighbourhood.title: Our Corner of Tallinn
neighbourhood.paragraph_one: Undercover sits on Kivimurru — Quarry Street — at the edge of Sikupilli, the oldest pocket of Lasnamäe. It's a neighbourhood that surprises Tallinn newcomers: early-1900s wooden houses lean shoulder-to-shoulder with later limestone blocks, and the cliff that gave the street its name drops away just behind us, opening a wide view toward Kadriorg's chestnut canopy and the bay beyond.
neighbourhood.paragraph_two: It's quieter here than the centre, but never far from it. The Majaka tram stop is a five-minute walk — trams 2 and 4 reach the Old Town in roughly fifteen minutes — and Ülemiste Centre, with its shops, cafés and the Skywheel of Tallinn, is one short ride south. Kadriorg Park, the Maarjamäe museums and Pirita's beach are an easy bus ride to the north. Around the corner you'll find small bakeries and lunch spots, a Selver for the essentials, and the green slopes of the old Lasnamäe quarry just down the hill — a good place to stretch your legs between calls.
